content.overview: A propagation specialist must separate whether a seed is alive from how quickly and uniformly it germinates and whether it establishes a normal seedling.

sections.title: Viability and vigor answer different questions
sections.body: Viability concerns whether seed tissue can still produce a living seedling; vigor concerns performance such as speed, uniformity and stress tolerance. A viable lot can still establish unevenly.

sections.title: Use denominators and time
sections.body: A germination result is interpretable only when the number tested, the number germinated and the observation window are preserved. Raw counts without denominators can mislead.

sections.title: Contamination can confound performance
sections.body: Research germination systems may use sterilization or antimicrobial treatments to reduce contamination. Such methods must be documented separately from seed-intrinsic performance.

commonMistakes: Treating a research protocol value as a universal production target.
Reporting successful seedlings without preserving the original denominator.
Changing multiple variables at once and then claiming one caused the result.
content.practicalApplication: Compare two seed-lot records with equal final germination percentage but different timing and uniformity; identify what additional evidence is needed before calling performance equivalent.
content.summary: Use source-controlled evidence, preserve identity and denominators, and keep observations separate from explanations.
